Shyam Metalics Signs MoU for Rs 50,000 Cr Steel Plant

October 5, 2026October 5, 2026
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:01
Instaread

Shyam Metalics signed a non-binding MoU with Maharashtra for a Rs 50,000 cr, 9 MTPA steel plant in Chandrapur.

Because the MoU is non-binding, the plant is still a plan. The company has started seeking approvals, clearances and incentives from the state, and the project moves ahead only if those come through.

It will be built in two phases. The first will make 3.75 million tonnes of finished steel a year. The second will add 5.25 million tonnes.

Everything will happen on a single site, from converting raw materials to melting, casting and rolling the steel.

The company says the output is aimed at construction, railways, carmakers and the oil and gas industry.

Iron ore comes from Gadchiroli, coal from the Chandrapur mining belt, and the region also has limestone and dolomite. The site is well connected by rail, road and power.

The company expects around 30,000 jobs, of which 10,000 would be direct and 20,000 indirect.

It also expects suppliers, fabrication units and transport firms in Vidarbha to gain from the plant.

On the environment side, Shyam Metalics plans to recover waste heat to generate power, use a dry method to cool coke and save water, and treat and reuse water in a closed loop.

In its exchange filing, the company said the Maharashtra government is not a related party. No promoter or key manager holds any interest in the deal.

The Chandrapur plan adds to expansion the firm announced earlier in Odisha, West Bengal and Jharkhand.

According to sources, it has also outlined about Rs 10,000 crore of capital spending over three to four years across carbon steel, stainless steel and aluminium, and targets revenue above Rs 42,000 crore by 2031.

Final incentive terms and state approvals are still pending.

Hacker Group Claims Access to 3.8 Lakh SBI Data Entries

Ali WaghbakriwalaOctober 21, 2026October 21, 2026
October 21, 2026October 21, 2026

The State Bank of India (SBI) is investigating a suspected data exposure after a hacker group called Siriusim claimed to have obtained around 3.8 lakh data entries linked to the country’s largest public sector lender.

The alleged dataset reportedly includes customer details, loan applications and account-opening documents. SBI has identified 3,897 records containing personal information in the material reviewed so far.

According to reports, the hacker group claims to possess approximately 3.75 lakh records in CSV format and 2,722 PDF documents. The material allegedly includes names, mobile numbers, dates of birth, email addresses, residential addresses and banking-related application records.

However, the reported number of entries does not necessarily represent the same number of individual customers, as multiple records may relate to one person. SBI’s preliminary examination identified 3,897 records containing personally identifiable information, while the authenticity and source of the wider dataset remain under investigation.

SBI reported that it was alerted to a potential cybersecurity incident on October 16 by its threat intelligence partner, the Defence Cyber Agency and CERT-In. In response, the bank initiated its internal security protocols and brought in an independent cybersecurity firm to examine the matter and assess any possible risks.

The bank clarified in its regulatory disclosure that the incident has not caused any significant disruption to its operations or business continuity. It also stated that there has been no material effect on its financial performance. The investigation is expected to establish the authenticity of the records, how the data may have been exposed and the potential risks to customers.

The alleged exposure highlights the growing risks banks face from cyberattacks and unauthorised access to customer information. Personal details can be misused in phishing attempts, identity fraud and scams involving people impersonating bank officials.

Customers should avoid sharing OTPs, PINs or passwords, remain cautious of unexpected calls and messages, and contact SBI through official channels if they notice suspicious activity.

The investigation’s findings will be important in determining the full extent of the incident and any further steps needed to protect affected customers.

Grauer & Weil Signs MoU With RENA Technologies for Solar JV

Tabassum ChaudharyOctober 20, 2026October 20, 2026
October 20, 2026October 20, 2026

Grauer & Weil (India) signed an MoU with RENA Technologies on 20 October to form a JV in the solar manufacturing value chain.

The company disclosed the agreement in a regulatory filing on Tuesday. Under it, the two firms will set up a new company together.

A joint venture is a separate company that two partners own and run together. This one will focus on the solar manufacturing chain.

Nothing is final yet. An MoU is a first step, not a full contract. The detailed terms will come in later agreements, and the company will disclose them once those are signed.

The partners plan to share control equally. Grauer & Weil and RENA will have equal rights in managing and governing the new venture.

RENA, a German technology firm, will license its proprietary technology to the venture. In return, it will receive a royalty, but the amount has not been agreed.

No shares have been issued under the MoU, and no loans are involved. The filing lists the deal size as not applicable at this preliminary stage.

Grauer & Weil said RENA has no link to its promoters, promoter group or group companies.

So the deal is not a related-party transaction. The two firms have no shareholding ties today.

Grauer & Weil works across chemicals, engineering, paints, lubricants and real estate.

Shareholders met for the company’s 68th annual general meeting on 17 September, held by video conferencing with Chairman Umeshkumar More presiding.

They approved a final dividend of Re 0.50 per share for the year ended 31 March 2026.

All eight resolutions passed with the required majority. The auditors gave clean opinions on the FY26 accounts.

Public institutions voted against the pay revisions for Aman More and Yash More, but both revisions still passed.

Rohitkumar More was reappointed as Whole-time Director for five years from 1 April 2027.

Transrail Lighting to Buy 49% in Solar Firm for Rs 20 Crore

Tabassum ChaudharyOctober 20, 2026October 20, 2026
October 20, 2026October 20, 2026

Transrail Lighting will invest up to Rs 20 crore for a 49% stake in NOPL Pace Green Energy, marking its entry into solar power.

The company disclosed the board’s decision to the exchanges in a filing on Monday, 19 October. It will pay in cash.

Until now, Transrail has focused on engineering and building projects for clients. This deal takes it into producing power.

It expects to help build the solar plants and own them over the long term. Once they run, they could bring in regular income.

NOPL is developing about 990 MW of solar capacity in Maharashtra under the Centre’s PM-KUSUM scheme.

The plants will feed farm power lines, so farmers get electricity for irrigation during the day.

The project already has a buyer. Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company Ltd (MSEDCL) has signed a 25-year agreement to take the power at a fixed Rs 3.10 per unit.

The total project cost stands at around Rs 3,900 crore. A financial institution has approved debt funding, subject to conditions.

Transrail will hold 49% at the start, and Onix Renewable Ltd keeps the other 51%. Even so, agreements give Transrail financial and project management control.

It can lift its stake to as much as 100% if both sides agree terms and approvals arrive.

NOPL was set up in April 2024 and has not started operations. It reported no revenue from operations in FY25 or FY26.

Randeep Narang, Transrail’s Managing Director and CEO, called the move a step towards working across the energy chain, from generation to transmission and distribution.

He said projects like this can bring more predictable long-term revenue and margins.

Completion needs government approvals and the lender’s consent. The company expects to finish within 180 days of NOPL’s board approval.

On 14 October, Transrail reported new orders worth Rs 408 crore, lifting this year’s order wins to Rs 2,429 crore.

In September, it raised its conductor-making capacity at the Silvassa plant by 70% to 40,800 km a year.

Gallantt Ispat Q2 Profit Falls 32% Despite Higher Revenue

Tabassum ChaudharyOctober 20, 2026October 20, 2026
October 20, 2026October 20, 2026

Gallantt Ispat’s Q2 profit fell 32% to Rs 60.51 crore due to higher costs, despite revenue rising 13% to Rs 1,145.89 crore.

The steelmaker told the stock exchanges that its board approved the unaudited consolidated results on 19 October.

They cover the three months ended 30 September. A year earlier, profit after tax stood at Rs 88.92 crore.

Sales moved the other way. Revenue from operations climbed from Rs 1,012.78 crore a year earlier, and total income reached Rs 1,164.04 crore, up from Rs 1,025.97 crore.

Costs ate the gain. Total expenses jumped to Rs 1,080.87 crore from Rs 922.95 crore.

Raw materials cost Rs 794.21 crore, up from Rs 730.28 crore. Goods bought for resale shot up to Rs 98.87 crore from just Rs 5.10 crore.

Operating profit, known as EBITDA, fell 16.6% to Rs 109.6 crore from Rs 131.5 crore a year earlier.

The operating margin, which shows how much of each rupee of sales the company keeps as operating profit, slipped to 9.57% from 13%.

Profit before tax dropped to Rs 83.17 crore from Rs 103.01 crore a year earlier. Earnings per share fell to Rs 2.51 from Rs 3.62.

The April to June quarter looked different. Profit then was Rs 123.67 crore, while revenue stayed almost flat at about Rs 1,146 crore.

Over the full six months, revenue rose to Rs 2,291.55 crore from Rs 2,140.52 crore.

Profit moved down to Rs 184.17 crore from Rs 262.72 crore. Half-year earnings per share slipped to Rs 7.63 from Rs 10.82.

Looking ahead, the company is lifting steelmaking capacity from 1 million tonnes to 1.29 million tonnes, with the new capacity targeted for the second half of FY27.

It is also developing its own iron ore mines to secure raw material supply. For now, the numbers show higher sales and lower earnings.

Mehul Telecom Opens Nine Franchise Stores Across Gujarat

Tabassum ChaudharyOctober 20, 2026October 20, 2026
October 20, 2026October 20, 2026

Mehul Telecom has opened nine franchise mobile stores across Gujarat in ten days, with the newest one launching in Visnagar on 20 October.

The Visnagar outlet, in Mahesana district, began trading on 20 October. It is the ninth store the Rajkot-based company has opened since 11 October.

The rollout came in waves. Morbi and Vatva in Ahmedabad opened first, on 11 October, and Chikhli in Navsari followed the next day.

Pranchi and Kodinar, both in Gir Somnath, started trading on 16 October. Gariadhar in Bhavnagar, Rajula in Amreli and Narol in Ahmedabad all opened together on 18 October.

Two outlets opened in Ahmedabad and Gir Somnath each, with single stores in Morbi, Navsari, Bhavnagar, Amreli, and Mahesana across 7 districts.

Two shop names are in use. Mobile Daddy appears on four of the new stores, in Morbi, Vatva, Pranchi and Gariadhar.

The other five, in Chikhli, Kodinar, Rajula, Narol and Visnagar, carry the Mehul Telecom name.

All nine are ground-floor shops. The Visnagar one is at Sanskrut Square, near Mahesana Chokdi.

The Kodinar shop stands beside the ST bus stand, and the Rajula shop is close to the police station.

Mehul Telecom told the BSE about the openings in notices under SEBI’s listing rules.

The company began in May 2023 and sells phones through a mix of shops it runs itself and shops run by franchise partners. Its registered office is in Rajkot.

Inside these stores, shoppers find smartphones and tablets, along with smartwatches, earphones, chargers, power banks, phone covers and warranty plans.

The brand list covers Samsung, iPhone, Vivo, Oppo, Realme, OnePlus, Redmi, Nothing, Tecno, Infinix and Nokia.

Business Remedies reported the first three stores, in Morbi, Vatva and Chikhli, on 13 October. Six more opened in the days after.

With Visnagar open, the company has launched nine stores across seven districts in just ten days.
